deficiencies.description: The source says that bone tumours lead to erosion of bone function, whereas the rewrite says that they erode the bone itself.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: And things like if tumors in bones lead to erosion of that bone function, so you can get fractures
deficiencies.rewritePassage: Tumours in bones lead to erosion of the bone, so that fractures can occur

considerations.sourcePassage: Well, as I was hinting at, it interferes with normal functions. So a lump growing in the wrong place will cause pressure and blockage. And if you think about them in the different settings in which they occur, things like a meningioma will cause pressure. Things like a lung carcinoma will cause blockage.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the explanation that cancer disrupts normal function through pressure and blockage, together with the meningioma and lung carcinoma examples.

considerations.sourcePassage: And then within the airways, this builds up secretions within the lungs, makes it harder for people to breathe, is a breeding ground for infection. And you can get pneumonia, which can lead to sepsis and death.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the full causal sequence from airway blockage through retained secretions and infection to pneumonia, sepsis and death.

considerations.sourcePassage: Things like obstruction of the bile ducts in the liver interferes with digestion.
considerations.reason: This effect is retained without a material change in meaning.

considerations.sourcePassage: and this causes an immense amount of pain. Bone pain is terrible.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the lecturer's point about the severity of pain caused by fractures and bone involvement.

considerations.sourcePassage: Also ulceration, you saw that enormous cauliflower structure within the colon. This causes a lot of bleeding and can lead to anemia.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves ulceration, the cauliflower-like colonic structure, bleeding and the risk of anaemia; the British spelling does not change the content.

considerations.sourcePassage: And also this competition with the normal, if you have a tumor that is occurring in some of the blood compartments, the hematopoietic stem cells that are there, these will interfere. This niche is not very big. This will interfere with your bone marrow, and it will result in things like infection and anemia as well.
considerations.reason: The rewrite resolves the disfluent wording as competition between the tumour and normal haematopoietic tissue, while preserving the limited niche, bone-marrow interference, infection and anaemia.

considerations.sourcePassage: And also there are general metabolic effects of having cancer, including cachexia, which is wasting, and also specific, depending on the tumor that you have, the tumor can make specific products itself.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains both general metabolic effects, including cachexia, and tumour-specific product formation.

considerations.sourcePassage: Right. So these primary tumors, where they're located, don't generally cause death. Only 10% of these deaths, generally, if they're occurring in things like the meningioma that I was telling you about or in the liver.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the claim that primary tumours account for only about 10% of deaths and retains the meningioma and liver examples.

considerations.sourcePassage: But you can get overwhelming death by secondary metastases colonizing organs all over the body. So when the tumor has spread all throughout the body, you can get things like liver failure. As I said, the bone marrow will fail altogether, and you'll succumb to infection and bleeding and erosion of bones will lead to skeletal collapse.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the contrast with widespread secondary metastases and the consequences of liver failure, bone-marrow failure, infection, bleeding and skeletal collapse.

considerations.sourcePassage: So there's lots of pain and debilitation, and it becomes difficult to breathe, and people end up with pneumonia, and they die.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the stated terminal consequences of pain, debilitation, breathing difficulty, pneumonia and death.
